plans.hypothesis: Blind cave species in America are phylogenetically nearer to surface species of America than to European cave species, and likewise for Europe.
plans.pass_criterion: In a time-calibrated phylogeny of cave taxa with surface relatives, at least 80% of troglobitic lineages have their nearest surface relative on the same continent, and fewer than 20% cluster with cave lineages from the other continent.
plans.fail_criterion: Fewer than 60% of troglobitic lineages have their nearest relative on the same continent, or cave lineages cluster across continents more than expected by chance (permutation p<0.05).
plans.interpretation: Darwin's 'affinities' means phylogenetic nearest relatives; 'blind cave animals' means troglobites. No single public dataset with cave-status plus phylogeny was found and fetched.
plans.no_dataset_reason: I did not find and fetch a single public dataset that combines troglobite status, continent and phylogenetic placement. Naming one would risk a fabricated identifier.

plans.hypothesis: Naturalised plants add proportionally more new genera than new species to regional floras, relative to native genus and species counts.
plans.pass_criterion: Across regions, (new genera / native genera) exceeds (new species / native species) by a factor of at least 1.5 in at least 75% of regions.
plans.fail_criterion: The ratio is below 1.1, or the genus-level gain is not larger in a majority of regions.
plans.interpretation: New genera are genera not present among natives of the region. This requires native counts per region, which a naturalised-only database does not supply.
plans.no_dataset_reason: GloNAF (glonaf.org) lists naturalised taxa only. Native genus and species counts per region would need a second dataset, and the rules allow exactly one.

plans.hypothesis: Biotic composition similarity among regions is not predicted by climatic similarity.
plans.pass_criterion: Partial Mantel correlation between climate distance and biotic dissimilarity among regions, controlling for geographic distance, is below 0.2, with matched-climate regions (e.g. 25-35S in Australia, South Africa, South America) having Sorensen turnover above 0.9.
plans.fail_criterion: The partial Mantel correlation is at least 0.4, or matched-climate regions share more than 30% of genera.
plans.interpretation: Needs paired climate and biota data in one dataset. No single one was fetched.
plans.no_dataset_reason: No single fetched public dataset pairs regional biota composition with climate surfaces.

plans.hypothesis: Taxonomic composition of fossil faunas is more similar between consecutive stages than between widely separated stages.
plans.pass_criterion: Mean Jaccard or Simpson genus similarity between consecutive stages exceeds that between stages 5 or more apart by at least 0.2, with monotonic decline of similarity with separation (Spearman rho below -0.8).
plans.fail_criterion: Difference below 0.05, or Spearman rho above -0.3.
plans.interpretation: 'Formation' is reinterpreted as chronostratigraphic stage or time bin; 'related' is genus-level compositional overlap in occurrences.

plans.hypothesis: Cannon bones of ox, sheep and giraffe differ by a simple uniaxial stretch.
plans.pass_criterion: After scaling to equal length, the width ratio sheep/ox is 0.67 +/- 0.1 and giraffe/ox is 0.33 +/- 0.1, with Procrustes residual after uniaxial affine fit below 5% of centroid size.

plans.hypothesis: Left and right horns of ruminants are mirror-image spirals.
plans.pass_criterion: After reflecting the left horn, landmark Procrustes distance to the right horn is below 5% of horn length in at least 90% of specimens.
plans.fail_criterion: Fewer than 60% of specimens fall below 10%.
plans.interpretation: Mirror symmetry is tested by left-right landmark asymmetry. My search found no public horn-specific 3D dataset.
plans.no_dataset_reason: No public bovid horn dataset was found; the only horn-specific hit was an access-restricted thesis.

plans.hypothesis: The length-weight constant k = W/L^3 varies systematically with length during growth, revealing changes of form.
plans.pass_criterion: Within species, the slope of log W on log L differs from 3.0 by more than 0.1 (95% CI excluding 3) in at least 70% of species.
plans.fail_criterion: Slope within 3.0 +/- 0.05 for at least 70% of species, i.e. k is constant.
plans.interpretation: k is the Fulton condition factor. The claim that k tracks form change is tested as k varying with L, which could also reflect condition rather than form.

plans.hypothesis: Blind cave species in America are phylogenetically nearer to surface species of America than to European cave species, and likewise for Europe.
plans.pass_criterion: In a time-calibrated phylogeny of cave taxa with surface relatives, at least 80% of troglobitic lineages have their nearest surface relative on the same continent, and fewer than 20% cluster with cave lineages from the other continent.
plans.fail_criterion: Fewer than 60% of troglobitic lineages have their nearest relative on the same continent, or cave lineages cluster across continents more than expected by chance (permutation p<0.05).
plans.interpretation: Darwin's 'affinities' means phylogenetic nearest relatives; 'blind cave animals' means troglobites. No single public dataset with cave-status plus phylogeny was found and fetched.
plans.no_dataset_reason: I did not find and fetch a single public dataset that combines troglobite status, continent and phylogenetic placement. Naming one would risk a fabricated identifier.

plans.hypothesis: Naturalised plants add proportionally more new genera than new species to regional floras, relative to native genus and species counts.
plans.pass_criterion: Across regions, (new genera / native genera) exceeds (new species / native species) by a factor of at least 1.5 in at least 75% of regions.
plans.fail_criterion: The ratio is below 1.1, or the genus-level gain is not larger in a majority of regions.
plans.interpretation: New genera are genera not present among natives of the region. This requires native counts per region, which a naturalised-only database does not supply.
plans.no_dataset_reason: GloNAF (glonaf.org) lists naturalised taxa only. Native genus and species counts per region would need a second dataset, and the rules allow exactly one.

plans.hypothesis: Biotic composition similarity among regions is not predicted by climatic similarity.
plans.pass_criterion: Partial Mantel correlation between climate distance and biotic dissimilarity among regions, controlling for geographic distance, is below 0.2, with matched-climate regions (e.g. 25-35S in Australia, South Africa, South America) having Sorensen turnover above 0.9.
plans.fail_criterion: The partial Mantel correlation is at least 0.4, or matched-climate regions share more than 30% of genera.
plans.interpretation: Needs paired climate and biota data in one dataset. No single one was fetched.
plans.no_dataset_reason: No single fetched public dataset pairs regional biota composition with climate surfaces.

plans.hypothesis: Taxonomic composition of fossil faunas is more similar between consecutive stages than between widely separated stages.
plans.pass_criterion: Mean Jaccard or Simpson genus similarity between consecutive stages exceeds that between stages 5 or more apart by at least 0.2, with monotonic decline of similarity with separation (Spearman rho below -0.8).
plans.fail_criterion: Difference below 0.05, or Spearman rho above -0.3.
plans.interpretation: 'Formation' is reinterpreted as chronostratigraphic stage or time bin; 'related' is genus-level compositional overlap in occurrences.

plans.hypothesis: Oceanic islands lack Palaeozoic and Mesozoic rocks, so ocean basins and continents have kept their positions since the Silurian.
plans.pass_criterion: Fewer than 5% of mapped units on genuinely oceanic islands (volcanic origin, not continental fragments) have Palaeozoic or Mesozoic ages, and no Palaeozoic unit is found.
plans.fail_criterion: At least 20% of oceanic-island units are Mesozoic or older, or any Palaeozoic unit is found on a verified oceanic island.
plans.interpretation: 'Secondary' means Mesozoic. Oceanic islands are defined as never-attached volcanic islands. Modern plate tectonics shows ocean floor is Jurassic or younger, so the stated inference about fixed oceans is expected to fail even if the island observation holds.

plans.hypothesis: Fossil preservation is strongly biased against soft-bodied taxa.
plans.pass_criterion: Taxa with no mineralised skeleton make up less than 5% of fossil genera in PBDB outside Lagerstatten, versus more than 30% of living marine genera, a ratio of at least 6 times.

plans.hypothesis: Conserved cellular machinery is shared across all domains of life.
plans.pass_criterion: At least 50 orthologous protein families are present in at least 95% of sampled genomes across the three domains.
plans.fail_criterion: Fewer than 10 such universal families.
plans.interpretation: 'Chemical composition, cellular structure' is mapped to universally conserved genes. No single dataset was fetched.
plans.no_dataset_reason: I did not fetch a single dataset decisive for universal-gene sharing, so none is named.

plans.hypothesis: Oceanic islands have a high endemic proportion despite low richness.
plans.pass_criterion: Median endemic proportion across oceanic islands exceeds 30% and is higher than for continental areas of equal size.
plans.fail_criterion: Median endemic proportion below 10%, or not higher than that for equal-area mainland.
plans.interpretation: Needs island native and endemic counts and area. The candidate Dryad island dataset I fetched has native/alien/extinct status but no endemism field.
plans.no_dataset_reason: No fetched dataset gives endemic and native counts with island area. GIFT's landing page rendered no description.

plans.hypothesis: Woody species (trees) are dioecious or monoecious more often than herbaceous species.
plans.pass_criterion: Proportion of species with separated sexes (dioecy plus monoecy) is higher in woody than herbaceous species, with odds ratio at least 1.5 and p<0.01.
plans.fail_criterion: Odds ratio at or below 1.1, or the herbaceous proportion is higher.
plans.interpretation: Dataset woody category stands for 'trees'. Darwin's claim was for England and he cited Hooker's counterexample for Australia, so check regional subsets too.

plans.hypothesis: Cell walls in tissue sections meet in threes at about 120 degrees regardless of cell size.

plans.fail_criterion: Mean angle deviates by more than 10 degrees, or |r| is above 0.4.
plans.interpretation: Requires measured junction angles from segmented tissue images. No such dataset was fetched.

plans.hypothesis: Within a species, right- and left-handed parastichy directions are about equally frequent.
plans.pass_criterion: Share of clockwise heads is within 45-55% and a binomial test fails to reject p=0.5 (p>0.05).
plans.fail_criterion: Share outside 40-60%, or binomial p<0.01.
plans.interpretation: Thompson's data were Norway spruce cones. The sunflower dataset tests the generalisation in another species, so a pass would not replicate the spruce figures (224 vs 243).
